count-120: count a group of objects and write the number.
count forward from any number up to 120 and say what number comes next.
read and write numbers to 120 and match number words to numerals.
count on to add and count back to subtract.
add-subtract-10: add two numbers with a sum up to 10.
find the number that goes with another number to make 10.
break a number up to 10 into two parts and find a missing part.
add-subtract-20: add within 20 by making a ten, using doubles, or counting on.
subtract within 20 by counting back, going back to 10, or thinking addition.
change the order of addends and add three numbers by finding a ten first.
use an addition fact to solve a related subtraction fact.
equal-sign: tell whether an equation is true or false by checking that both sides are the same amount.
find the unknown number in an addition or subtraction equation.
find a number that makes both sides of an equation the same, such as 6 + 4 = 5 + ___.
word-problems-20: solve stories where some are added or taken away.
solve stories about two parts and a total.
solve stories that ask how many more or how many fewer.
solve stories where the start or the change is unknown.
solve stories that add three numbers with a total up to 20.
tens-ones: make a ten from ten ones and tell how many tens and ones are in a group.
show a number from 11 to 19 as one ten and some ones.
count by tens and tell how many tens are in 10, 20, 30, … 90.
tell how many tens and ones are in a two-digit number and show it with blocks.
compare-numbers: tell which of two numbers is greater by comparing the tens first, then the ones.
write a comparison using the symbols >, =, and <.
find numbers that make a comparison true and explain my thinking.
add-subtract-100: find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number without counting by ones.
add tens to a two-digit number and subtract tens from tens.
add a one-digit number to a two-digit number when no new ten is made.
add a one-digit number to a two-digit number when the ones make a new ten.
add two two-digit numbers within 100 by adding tens and tens and ones and ones.
measuring-length: compare two lengths and put three objects in order from shortest to longest.
use a third object to compare two lengths.
measure a length by counting same-size units laid end to end.
tell when a measurement is wrong because of gaps, overlaps, or units of different sizes.
telling-time: tell and write time to the hour on analog and digital clocks.
tell and write time to the half hour on analog and digital clocks.
match analog and digital times and tell what time it will be one hour or half an hour later.
data: sort objects into up to three groups and use tally marks to show how many.
read how many are in each category of a picture graph, tally chart, or table.
find the total and tell how many more or fewer are in one category than another.
shapes-equal-shares: tell which attributes make a shape what it is (closed, number of sides and corners) and which do not (color, size, position).
name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles, trapezoids, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and rectangular prisms.
put shapes together to make new shapes and tell how many shapes I used.
split circles and rectangles into 2 or 4 equal shares and name halves, fourths, and quarters.
describe a whole as two halves or four fourths and explain that more equal shares are smaller shares.
